claim: With m2 fixed at 0.5, the N=64 to N=128 drop in trained force R2 does not go away. At N=128 (best layer 4), trained force R2 is 0.693 (seed 20) and 0.684 (seed 21), against 0.763 and 0.789 for the same seeds in the paired N=64 m2-fixed arm. That is a drop of 0.070 and 0.105, close to the wide-m2 drop of 0.08-0.13. The force controls barely move (seed 20: about 0.63 to 0.630; seed 21: about 0.594 to 0.583, change of 0.012 or less), so the whole drop is in trained R2. The force margin falls from 0.133/0.195 to 0.063/0.101, and seed 20 no longer beats its control. In contrast, accel_step stays strong: R2 0.945/0.933 vs control 0.793/0.760, margin 0.152/0.173, headroom-normalised margin 0.74/0.72. Layer-1 distance R2 falls only a little (0.950/0.926 to 0.915/0.908). The force loss at N=128 is therefore in reading out 1/r^2, not in the m2 factor.
confidence_note: Both seeds completed all 3000 steps and both show a drop of at least 0.06 with flat controls, which matches the expected-if-false outcome. The N=64 baseline values (0.763/0.789) come from the paired arm's earlier finding, not from probes_final of this experiment. The paired-arm trajectory gives 0.768 for seed 20, which may be the max-over-layers field. N=64 controls were inferred as R2 minus margin. Seed 20's drop (0.070) is only 0.01 above the 0.06 bar, so a probes_final N=64 value below 0.753 would make that seed inconclusive. The best layers also differ for seed 21: force peaks at layer 1 (the distance layer) at N=64 and at layer 4 at N=128, so part of the drop may be a layer-1 force signal that disappears. The comparison is at matched training step, not matched loss (N=128 val_mse_ratio is 0.048-0.056). The verdict would change if the drop shrinks below 0.03 when both arms are read at matched val_mse_ratio, or if more seeds (22-23) show drops under 0.06.
